messages:
maria: Quick sync: we've seen a pattern where brand-new shards (recently created or after reboot) briefly spike as the lowest-latency option and then blow out. Ops wants a principled mitigation rather than ad-hoc exclusions. Thoughts on an "entropy floor" vs a probabilistic admission/hedging approach?
lee: Data note: most of these are < 5m old. They win because initial queue=0 gives great p50/p95. But sample count ~ 1-3 requests.
hana: We should treat small-n as high-uncertainty. Two families of fixes: 1) deterministic score penalty based on sample_count (frequentist shrinkage), 2) probabilistic selection that injects randomness proportional to uncertainty so we avoid cliff effects.
sam: Also consider admission tokens: allow N concurrent requests to cold shard, then steer overflow elsewhere. That lets shard warm without being overwhelmed.
maria: I sketched a combined approach: entropy_floor to avoid overconfident ranking + hedged admission tokens for smooth warmups. Proposed runtime primitives: shrinkage_adjust(p95, n, prior), entropy_floor(min_entropy), admit_tokens(k, ttl). Policy remains declarative.
lee: Example policy snippet:
```
scorer {
  base_latency: p95_latency
  adjusted: shrinkage_adjust(base_latency, sample_count, prior=global_p95)
  score: max(adjusted, entropy_floor(0.12)) + cost * 0.8
}
routing_policy {
  admission: admit_tokens(5, ttl=30s)  // only for shards with n < 50
}
```
hana: shrinkage_adjust will move small-n p95 toward global prior; it's basically Bayesian-ish. entropy_floor ensures no shard looks 'too good'. Two knobs — the prior and the floor — cover different failure modes.
sam: Implementation constraints: shrinkage_adjust must be O(1) and use precomputed priors per model+seq_len bucket. admit_tokens is best implemented inside the serving runtime with lightweight counters (leaky-bucket style).
devops-bot: Telemetry: can emit per-shard tags: sample_count, prior_used, entropy_score, admission_tokens_in_use. I can add a dashboard template. :sparkles:
maria: UX question: how will tenants see this? We need defaults that preserve cheap-tier routing for tenants that opt in. Suggest exposing two toggles in tenant config: coldstart_mode = {conservative, default, aggressive} and per-tenant admit_override.
lee: Good. Conservative -> higher entropy_floor and smaller admit_tokens. Aggressive -> lower floor, larger tokens. Default sits between.
hana: Eval plan: run three sims on 30d telemetry: (A) current, (B) shrinkage+entropy_floor, (C) shrinkage+entropy+admit_tokens. Measure selection stability, post-selection tail latency, and cost delta.
sam: For canary rollout: implement runtime primitives behind feature flag, shadow route scoring for 1w, then enable admit_tokens with low k on 1% traffic, monitor regressions.
maria: Danger: admit_tokens could create per-shard hotspots if k is too high; also admitting too many can hide systemic load issues. Mitigate via cross-shard token pool fallback. If local tokens exhausted, route elsewhere.
devops-bot: Note: populate alerts for token_exhaustion_rate, cross_shard_fallback_rate, and cost-per-token change.
lee: Question about policy DSL surface: do we expose entropy_floor(min_value) as a primitive grammar token or should it be a runtime default? DSL exposure helps power users but adds surface area.
hana: I vote runtime default + optional DSL override. Keep language small; runtime exposes safe primitive with tenant override API.
sam: Edge-case: what if global prior is stale because model/seq changed? Use per-model+seq rolling priors and a decay. Also add a manual override when we onboard a new model.
maria: Action items we agreed:
- runtime: implement shrinkage_adjust and admit_tokens primitives, plus config hooks for entropy_floor (sam)
- telemetry: add shard-level tags and dashboard template (devops-bot -> maria)
- experiments: run the 3-arm sim and shadow scoring (lee)
- policy: document recommended tenant settings and DSL opt-in (hana)
- rollout: feature-flagged canary with token k=2 on 1% traffic (sam/lee)
- docs: short explainer why we add entropy floor + admit tokens to avoid product support questions (maria)

maria: timeline: prototype primitives in 1 sprint, sim in parallel, shadow scoring in sprint+1, canary in sprint+2. If sim shows big cost regressions we'll back off.
devops-bot: Reminder — SLA tenants should continue to respect explicit affinity rules; feature-flag default won't override hard tenant affinity.
lee: One more idea: instrument a quick "regret estimator" that computes predicted vs observed latency when new shard chosen. That will be handy for tuning floor/prior.
hana: Agreed. If regret estimator shows systematic bias, increase prior weight or raise entropy floor.
sam: I'll file GH issues for runtime work and mark them P1 for this quarter.
maria: Thanks all. We'll sync in the next arch check-in with sim results. :white_check_mark:
